title: RO-MT081-RoleSchemaAndRegistry

scope.summary:
GOAL: Create the hsk.handshake_role@1 typed schema and the PostgreSQL-backed Handshake Role registry — the foundation of the RO family. A Handshake Role is the productized successor of the repo-gov startup inject-prompts (.GOV/roles/* protocols): a versioned, operator-owned overlay definition that Handshake (and future projects built by Handshake) attach to agent sessions at launch. This MT delivers the data model, persistence, CRUD Rust API, HTTP routes, and a read-only IPC surface; injection mechanics (MT-082), composition (MT-083), importer (MT-084), GUI (MT-085), and child assignment (MT-086) all build on this registry.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New backend module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/handshake_roles.rs (schema types + HandshakeRoleStore), one new numbered migration under src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/ (handshake_roles tables), new HTTP route module src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/handshake_roles.rs registered in src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/mod.rs, swarm_orchestration/mod.rs re-export, plus backend tests. No frontend edits in this MT (GUI is MT-085).

DETAILED SPEC — hsk.handshake_role@1 record fields:
- id: kebab-case stable identifier (e.g. "orchestrator", "wp-validator"); regex ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$; unique.
- version: monotonic integer starting at 1. Role versions are IMMUTABLE once written; an edit creates version N+1. The registry answers "current version" and "specific version" lookups.
- title: short operator-facing display name.
- description: what the role is for, one paragraph.
- overlay_prompt: markdown text. This is the role body that will be OVERLAYED on top of harness defaults (Claude --append-system-prompt-file pattern), never a full system-prompt replacement.
- tool_policy: { allow: [tool-class strings], deny: [tool-class strings], transport_hints: { claude: {allowed_tools: [], disallowed_tools: []}, codex: {notes: string}, acp: {notes: string} } } — per-transport mapping hints because each transport expresses tool restriction differently.
- model_profile: { preferred_lane: string|null, preferred_model: string|null, effort: "low"|"medium"|"high"|null } — advisory routing profile consumed by the composition engine (MT-083) and spawn flow (MT-086).
- transport_bindings: { claude: "APPEND_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE"|"AGENTS_JSON", codex: "FIRST_TURN_PREFIX", acp: "FIRST_PROMPT_SEGMENT" } — strategy enums per transport; defaults claude=APPEND_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE, codex=FIRST_TURN_PREFIX, acp=FIRST_PROMPT_SEGMENT. Enum variants are closed; FULL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_REPLACEMENT deliberately does not exist.
- provenance: { source: "operator"|"imported", source_ref: string|null } — imported roles (MT-084) carry the source protocol path + content hash in source_ref.
- status: "draft"|"active"|"retired". Only active roles are injectable. draft->active requires an explicit approve transition (operator surface in MT-085); active->retired is terminal for that version lineage.

Rust surface in handshake_roles.rs: pub struct HandshakeRole (serde, mirrors schema), pub enum RoleStatus, pub enum ClaudeRoleBinding/CodexRoleBinding/AcpRoleBinding, pub struct HandshakeRoleStore { pool: PgPool } following the ModelLaneStore persistence pattern in src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs (sqlx typed queries, EventLedger append per mutation, FlightRecorder wiring). Store methods: create_role, new_version, get_role (id + optional version, default current), list_roles (status filter), activate_role, retire_role. Every mutation appends a typed ledger event (handshake_role_created / handshake_role_version_added / handshake_role_activated / handshake_role_retired) with role id + version + overlay sha256, so role changes are ledgered and replayable.

Migration: next free NNNN number under src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/, table handshake_roles (id text, version int, title, description, overlay_prompt text, tool_policy jsonb, model_profile jsonb, transport_bindings jsonb, provenance jsonb, status text CHECK constraint, overlay_sha256 text, created_at timestamptz, PRIMARY KEY (id, version)) + partial unique index enforcing at most one active version per id; paired .down.sql per existing convention.

HTTP routes in src/api/handshake_roles.rs, registered in src/api/mod.rs: GET /api/roles (list, ?status= filter), GET /api/roles/{id} (current), GET /api/roles/{id}/versions/{version}, POST /api/roles (create draft), PUT /api/roles/{id} (new draft version), POST /api/roles/{id}/activate, POST /api/roles/{id}/retire. JSON bodies validate against hsk.handshake_role@1; malformed kebab id or unknown status is a 422 typed error.

IPC read surface: expose list_handshake_roles / get_handshake_role read-only commands through the same app bridge the swarm React components (app/src/components/swarm/) already consume, mirroring GET semantics only; write paths stay HTTP + native GUI. The React consumer itself lands in MT-085.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs to copy the store/persistence/event pattern (PgPool, sqlx::query, typed event append, SOURCE_COMPONENT const).
2. Author the migration pair (up/down) with the table + CHECK + one-active-version partial unique index; verify against the numbering convention in src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/.
3. Implement handshake_roles.rs types + HandshakeRoleStore with the six store methods; enforce kebab-case id and immutability (UPDATE of an existing (id,version) row is not exposed; new_version inserts).
4. Wire EventLedger append + FlightRecorder record for each mutation, including overlay_sha256 so downstream injection events (MT-082) can prove which bytes were approved.
5. Register the module in swarm_orchestration/mod.rs.
6. Implement src/api/handshake_roles.rs route handlers over the store; register the router in src/api/mod.rs next to the existing operator_chat routes.
7. Expose the two read-only IPC commands over the existing app bridge.
8. Tests: store CRUD round-trip against managed PostgreSQL; immutability negative test (second create of same (id,version) fails); one-active-version constraint test; status-transition matrix test (draft->active->retired legal; retired->active illegal); HTTP 422 on malformed id; ledger-event presence assertion per mutation.
9. Update the in-product UserManual with the roles-registry entry (purpose, routes, fields, failure modes) in the same change.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** except named IPC read surfaces
.GOV/** (role protocols are read-only source material; importer reads, never writes)
acceptance_criteria: hsk.handshake_role@1 Rust types exist with all nine field groups (id, version, title, description, overlay_prompt, tool_policy, model_profile, transport_bindings, provenance, status) and serde round-trip.
Migration applies and reverses cleanly on managed PostgreSQL; handshake_roles table enforces (id,version) PK, status CHECK, and at-most-one-active-version-per-id.
HandshakeRoleStore create/new_version/get/list/activate/retire all pass against live PostgreSQL; role versions are immutable (negative test proves overwrite fails).
Every store mutation appends a typed EventLedger event carrying role id, version, and overlay_sha256; replay reconstructs registry state.
HTTP routes GET/POST/PUT /api/roles* respond with typed JSON; malformed kebab id and illegal status transition return typed 4xx errors, not 500s.
transport_bindings enum has no full-system-prompt-replacement variant (compile-time closed enum; test asserts serialization surface).
Read-only IPC list/get commands return the same rows as the HTTP list/get routes.
In-product UserManual gains the handshake-roles-registry entry in the same change.
proof_targets: cargo sqlx migrate run && cargo sqlx migrate revert (or the project's managed-PG migration harness) applied against a live managed PostgreSQL
cargo test -p handshake_core handshake_roles_http -- --nocapture (route tests incl. 422 negatives)
expected_tests: store CRUD round-trip on live PG
implementation_notes: Persistence pattern to copy: ModelLaneStore in swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs (PgPool + sqlx + typed event constants + SOURCE_COMPONENT).
Do NOT store overlay files on disk in this MT; overlay_prompt lives in PG. Temp-file materialization for Claude injection is MT-082's job.
Roles are operator-authored/approved, model-consumed: no API path may silently auto-activate a draft; activation is always an explicit transition.

Verified field basis: Claude Code supports --append-system-prompt/--append-system-prompt-file and --agents '<json>' (named agent definitions with description/tools/model/permissionMode); Codex has no append flag (AGENTS.md + config.toml profiles + first-turn input); ACP has no system-prompt primitive. transport_bindings encodes exactly these three strategies.
Portability: no hardcoded absolute paths anywhere; DB access via existing pool config.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend schema/registry MT; the operator-facing Role Manager GUI is MT-085. Ledger events + HTTP routes provide the non-UI trace projection.

target_entries: handshake-roles-registry: purpose, hsk.handshake_role@1 fields, /api/roles* routes, IPC read commands, draft/active/retired lifecycle, failure/recovery (typed 4xx, migration rollback)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: internal_diagnostics/Palmistry not yet shipped in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1; record DEFERRED with integration follow-up per HBR-INT-009.

risk_if_missed: No typed role authority exists; every downstream RO MT (injection, composition, importer, GUI, child assignment, proofs) is blocked, and role text stays as unversioned repo-gov prose that cannot be productized or ledgered.

risks: RISK-1: Mutable role versions — an in-place UPDATE path lets an approved overlay silently change after activation, so injected sessions run text the operator never approved.
RISK-2: Shadow activation — a create/import path that defaults status to active bypasses operator approval and makes unreviewed prompts injectable.
RISK-3: Full-replacement creep — a transport_bindings variant or API field that permits whole-system-prompt replacement destroys harness agentic scaffolding (rejected by research).
RISK-4: Concurrent activation race — two parallel sessions activating different versions of the same role leave two active versions and nondeterministic injection.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): (id,version) primary key with insert-only store API; negative test proves overwrite of an existing version fails; overlay_sha256 recorded per version.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): status defaults to draft on every create path; activate is a distinct route/store method; test asserts POST /api/roles never yields active.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): closed Rust enums for transport_bindings with no replacement variant; grep proof target over the module.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): partial unique index (one active version per id) + transactional activate that demotes the prior active row; concurrency test with two parallel activates.

research_provenance.source: Verified role-injection field research (Claude Code --append-system-prompt/--append-system-prompt-file/--agents/--agent, full --system-prompt replacement rejected; Codex AGENTS.md/config.toml profiles/first-turn input; ACP no system-prompt primitive) + inspected product code: swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs ModelLaneStore persistence pattern, swarm_orchestration/operator_chat.rs OperatorChatLaunchService, migrations/ numbering convention + inspected .GOV/roles/* protocol structure (identity, duties, HBR gates, forbidden actions) as the source material Handshake Roles streamline.
corrections: Roles are overlays, never full system-prompt replacements — transport_bindings enum is closed by design.
Operator authors/approves roles, models consume them: draft-by-default + explicit activate transition is contract-level, not GUI courtesy.
Registry is provider-agnostic: per-transport strategy lives in transport_bindings/tool_policy.transport_hints, not in forked per-provider role records.
